purpose: Independent simulated beginner mouse-only RILL usability session; observations are limited to the visible UI.
persona: Simulated first-time RILL beginner interested in making a short melodic instrumental.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: The empty-track hint, instrument assignment, labeled piano-roll notes, exact loop duration and on-screen naming keyboard let me complete the composition and file workflows by mouse. Duplicate needed help and trimming needed a correction.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark teal arrangement, waveforms, note previews and moving meters looked coherent and readable. The restrained palette and similar clip colors were less visually distinctive.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Drawing, repeating and naming responded promptly, but playback recovery consumed extra steps and WAV export showed an elapsed-time wait before completion. This is a laboratory-session impression, not a hardware benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Moderate confusion: Duplicate initially appeared to be an immediate command; Tool help explained clicking a clip. One MIDI trim left 30.536 seconds and needed another attempt. The output failure persisted after following the suggested setup recovery.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The visible app provided audio arranging, a VST3 instrument, MIDI drawing, group duplication, trimming, mouse-only naming, project saving and both requested exports. Reliable sustained playback was not established in this session, and other plug-ins or advanced features were not evaluated.

findings.observation: The empty arranger hint said double-click for MIDI. Doing so opened the device library, and Assign instrument created a MIDI track labeled Rill Lab Sine.
Pencil drags created notes with pitch labels. Drawing beyond the original clip end visibly extended the clip. A four-bar rising and falling melody could be drawn without typing.

Play initially showed active audio and instrument meters and the playhead advanced from bar 1 to bar 4. A later warning said Audio output stream failed or disconnected; details named ALSA snd_pcm_avail_delay I/O error (5). Selecting Rill lab paced output in Audio setup, applying and trying Stop/Play returned the warning.
Clicking Duplicate selected a tool without immediately copying anything. Tool help explained clicking a clip; clicking a selected clip then duplicated both marquee-selected tracks together.

Trimming the last audio repeat worked, but the first MIDI trim left the project at 30.536 seconds. A small second trim aligned both tracks at 30.000 seconds. The loop end label provided precise timing feedback.
File > Rename project exposed a Keyboard button with clickable letters, Clear and Space. This allowed the chosen title luna loop; Save reused that title as the default filename.

The WAV dialog reported Arrangement 0:30. Disabling effect tails preserved that displayed duration. Both WAV and MIDI file pickers reused the project name, and each export eventually displayed an explicit Exported notice.
During WAV export the bottom status showed elapsed seconds. Attempts to open the File menu had no visible effect until export completed, and no remaining-time estimate was shown.

outcome.status: Completed through the visible composition, save and export workflows; playback encountered an unresolved laboratory output error and file contents remain independently unverified.
outcome.composition: A 112 BPM, 4/4, fourteen-bar instrumental arrangement: supplied Circuit rhythm audio repeated across the drum track, plus a manually drawn twelve-note rising/falling four-bar melody repeated on a MIDI instrument track with the final repeat trimmed to two bars. Both tracks and the loop end visibly align at 30.000 seconds.
outcome.instrument: Rill Lab Sine, shown as VST3 in the device library
outcome.playback_observed: Initially Pause was shown, the playhead advanced from bar 1 to bar 4 and both track meters were active. An audio output stream failed/disconnected warning later appeared. The suggested output-selection and Stop/Play recovery did not establish sustained playback. No audio was auditioned.

limitations: No file contents or heard audio claim; independent coordinator verification follows. Artifact paths are derived from visible native file dialogs and completion notices.

The timer-paced virtual audio backend and software graphics are laboratory conditions; observed output errors, elapsed export time and responsiveness should not be generalized to physical audio hardware.
Only the installed Rill Lab Sine VST3 instrument was assigned; results do not establish compatibility with other third-party plug-ins.
The supplied audio was reused and repeated. The melody was composed visually without listening, so musical quality and mix balance were not assessed.
